meta.title: Jota-Screen — You talk. The TV handles it.
meta.description: Jota-Screen turns the TV you already own into Jota's screen: it answers without covering what you watch, your phone is the remote, and everything stays on your network.

s1.headline: You talk. The TV handles it.
s1.subhead: The TV you already own, turned into Jota's screen.
s1.caption: Your TV, when nobody's using it.

s2.caption1: You're watching something. Jota answers up top, without pausing anything.
s2.caption2: And what it has pending stays in sight.

s3.caption1: When there's screen to spare, you see everything it does.
s3.caption2: It opens websites, plays music, launches whatever you ask.

s4.caption1: Nothing to install: it's a web page on your phone.
s4.caption2: Trackpad, keyboard, volume and Jota's voice.

s5.caption1: A code on the TV and you're in.
s5.caption2: You, your family and your guests, each with their own place.

s6.line1: A mini PC or that old laptop you no longer use, an HDMI cable and your phone.
s6.line2: Jota-Screen provides the screen; jota-gateway connects it to Jota's brain.
s6.soon: For now you install it by hand, following the READMEs.
s6.network: All on your network. Away from home, through the tunnel or proxy you choose.
s6.alt: Diagram: a mini PC or old laptop connects over HDMI to the TV; jota-gateway connects it to Jota's brain and to your phone.

meta.title: Jota, a voice assistant that lives in your home
meta.description: Jota runs on a machine of your own. Talk to it from the TV, a speaker or your phone. It works with what you already have: Home Assistant, OpenClaw and the AI model you choose.

hero.headline: A voice assistant that lives in your home.
hero.sub: Jota runs on a machine of your own. You talk to it from the TV, from a speaker or from your phone, and it works with what you already have: Home Assistant, OpenClaw and the AI model you choose.
hero.caption: You're watching a series and ask where it was filmed. Jota answers on the TV and the show keeps playing.
hero.tvLabel: The TV with Jota-Screen, answering a question about the show

house.title: It's all over the house
house.lead: Jota-Gateway is the brain. Every place you talk to it from is a client connected to it.
house.tvBody: Jota-Screen. A mini PC or an old laptop plugged in over HDMI. Your phone is the remote and the microphone, with no app to install.
house.tvLabel: The TV at rest, with the time and the weather
house.voiceTitle: On a speaker or a mic
house.voiceBody: jota-voice, open source, on a Mac, an Android or Linux. Say the wake word and talk; the answer plays right there.
house.voiceLabel: jota-voice listening to a dinner reminder
house.phoneBody: An app of its own, experimental and at an early stage.

keep.title: With what you already use
keep.lead: Jota sits on top of what you already have at home and takes it to the TV, the speaker and the phone.

rows.name: Home Assistant
rows.body: Jota talks to it over MCP and asks it for things around the house. It works the other way too: Home Assistant's voice assistant can be Jota.

rows.name: OpenClaw
rows.body: It's the brain, with its memory, its agents, its tools and its scheduled tasks.

rows.name: The AI model
rows.body: Local or in the cloud, whichever you pick in OpenClaw. If it's in the cloud, what you say reaches it already turned into text.

rows.name: The voice
rows.body: whisper.cpp and Kokoro on your network. Or ElevenLabs: if it transcribes, it gets your audio; if it speaks, it gets the text of the answers.

keep.protocol: Everything goes through Jota-Gateway. If you want to write your own client, the protocol is documented.

local.title: It runs on a machine of your own
local.body: Your voice never goes through a cloud service of ours. With jota-transcriber, jota-speaker and a local model, what you say never leaves your network.
local.open: The gateway, the transcription, the voice and jota-voice are open source.
local.link: What leaves home and what doesn't
